prompt_text: Who is the best healthcare marketing agency in St. Louis?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” healthcare marketing agency in St. Louis — the right agency depends on your organization’s size, goals, services needed, budget and timeline. I can, however, help you find the best fit. To do that quickly, tell me a few details:

- What type of organization are you (hospital system, physician group, clinic, medical device, biotech, behavioral health, senior care, etc.)?
- Primary goals (patient acquisition, physician recruitment, brand awareness, telehealth adoption, PR/crisis, internal communications, product launch)?
- Which services do you need (paid media, SEO, content, creative/branding, web design, social, analytics, reputation management, PR)?
- Approximate budget and timeline?
- Must-have requirements (HIPAA experience, bilingual outreach, local community ties, veteran-owned, minority-owned)?

If you want to start now without those details, here’s how to identify the best agency for healthcare specifically:

Key criteria to evaluate
- Healthcare experience: HIPAA/compliance knowledge, past work with hospitals/clinics/biotech or similar.
- Measurable results: case studies showing metrics (cost per acquisition, conversion lift, appointment growth, patient lifetime value).
- Digital capability: SEO, paid search & social, programmatic, analytics, and tracking across patient journeys.
- Creative + content: patient-focused messaging, physician recruitment campaigns, video and patient testimonial production.
- Reputation management: online reviews, local listings, and crisis/PR experience.
- Data & tech integration: EMR/appointment systems, CRM integration, attribution models.
- Local market knowledge: community outreach, referral network understanding, payer landscape familiarity.
- References and team: real client references, account team bios, and responsiveness.

Questions to ask agencies
- Can you show 2–3 healthcare case studies and the results?
- How do you handle HIPAA and patient data in campaigns?
- Which analytics and attribution tools do you use?
- How do you measure ROI for patient acquisition?
- Who would be on our account team and what’s the communication cadence?
- What is your pricing model and typical contract length?
- Can you provide local references?

Red flags
- No healthcare case studies or vague results.
- No compliance or patient-data procedures.
- Promises of guaranteed rankings or unrealistic timelines.
- Lack of measurement/attribution strategy.

If you want, I can:
- Research and send a tailored shortlist of St. Louis agencies with proven healthcare work (including summaries, relevant case studies, ballpark pricing, and client references).
- Provide an RFP template you can send to agencies and a simple scoring rubric to compare proposals.

Which would you prefer?
